releaseNotes:
Grocery Simulator is now Market Mania
The game has a new name. Your shop, your staff and your save are exactly as you left them.

At the till
A customer owed a rupee or two the till cannot make now waves it away, instead of leaving the desk stuck with nothing to press.
When the till cannot make the change at all, even with another note from the customer, they take their cash back and pay by card. Nobody leaves forty rupees behind any more.
Some customers hand over their odd rupees with the notes, so a 342 rupee sale is paid with 352. That is how coins find their way back into the till.
Cancel Sale is always there at your desk, while scanning and while being paid.
Leaving the desk and coming back no longer changes what the customer says about their change.
Patience starts again when a customer reaches the desk, so a long queue is not held against the one being served.

Your money
A save from before 5.2 had its takings counted in the balance and in the till. Loading it now takes that surplus out of the till, so banking it cannot count it twice.
A shelf can ask at most three times a product's usual price.

On the shop floor
Spills and customers needing help kept to the first day. They now come back every day.
A spill left overnight no longer costs reputation while the shop is empty.
A price check corrects the wrong shelf tag. It used to change your price to the wrong one.
A customer sent away from the counter puts back what they picked, and gets back any cash they had already paid.
A shoplifter who slips out while the gate is busy is announced, and the shelf stops holding space for what they took.
Customers stop asking for a product you have removed from the shelves, until you buy or shelve it again.
The mop keeps going if you walk away from the rack, and tells you when the spill is clean.

Settings and TalkBack
Volume settings are kept on their own. They work from the main menu before any game, and New Game no longer resets them.
MarketHub and StockPro only put you in the search box the first time you open them, not every time you come back from a product.
Fire Employee asks you to confirm first.
A deposit clearing no longer pulls TalkBack away while you are choosing notes for the next one.
Customer voices stop when you leave the store, instead of a queued line starting in the background, and they no longer fall silent for the rest of the session.
